newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian army units loyal to rival PMs clash.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian army units loyal to rival PMs clash.

text.p: Cambodian government army units loyal to the country's rival prime ministers clashed north of Phnom Penh on Wednesday, an army general said.
General Tom Sombol, a senior military adviser to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, said the clash occurred late in the afternoon following earlier shooting in the area.

The general said the latest fighting broke out when troops loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen tried to confiscate weapons from troops loyal to Ranariddh who had been involved in the earlier clash.
Tom Sombol said he had no details of casualties, but that the situation at Preak Kadam, 30 km (20 miles) north of the capital, remained tense.
"The situation is not so good," he told Reuters.
Earlier, General Mol Reup, a military adviser to Second Prime Minster Hun Sen, told Reuters the first clash had been sparked by a local dispute
"The fighting was not between FUNCINPEC and CPP," he said, referring to Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party and Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party.
Mol Reup said the first skirmish erupted late on Tuesday and continued into Wednesday after a dispute at an unofficial military checkpoint in the area.
One senior army officer was shot in the earlier clash but his condition was not known, Mol Reup said.
Security sources said forces from both sides were on alert in Phnom Penh.
Political tension was already high in the capital after several days of reports of troop movements in and around the city.
Hun Sen warned earlier this week that he would use force if he found Ranariddh's military men bringing troops into Phnom Penh illegally. Ranariddh denied he was moving troops into the city.
Security forces loyal to the two prime ministers fought a gun battle in central Phnom Penh on June 17 in which two of Ranariddh's bodyguards died.
